clue.text: Let's resend Busted. They're most unlike Fatboy Slim in the extreme

definitions.note: slim to the highest degree, a superlative adjective

indicators.note: something busted is broken apart, so these letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A boy band's second-rate tribute act are hardly a match for the big-beat DJ Fatboy Slim.
explanation.walkthrough: Busted is a British pop band, Fatboy Slim a DJ. 'They're most unlike Fatboy' is extra colour leading into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender is a synonym of slim, and the superlative form expresses slimness taken as far as it goes.

clue.text: Get lost in the rhythm, then I tango

parts.note: a beat is the pulse or rhythm of music
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer loses themselves in the music before a tango.
explanation.walkthrough: Beat It is also a Michael Jackson hit, fitting the music theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are curt idiomatic imperatives telling someone to go away at once.

clue.text: Group providing support for The Cars is back in the continent

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.words: Group providing support for The Cars
parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is the UK motoring group that rescues broken-down cars

indicators.note: back means the little word is read the other way round

explanation.surface: A support act opening for the American band The Cars makes a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cars is a band, and supporting a band means opening for it; here it is the AA's roadside rescue. Asia is also a rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the continents, home to China and India.

clue.text: Make bad fist of EP. Not the usual tracks

indicators.note: to make a bad job of something is to mangle it, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A band botches their extended-play record, departing from their usual songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracks' looks like songs on the EP, but the sense is ski runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing away from the groomed runs is skiing off the marked slopes, away from the normal tracks.

clue.text: Aguilera hasn't the heart to drop artist having fever

indicators.note: having no heart means the central letters of what is left go
to drop says some letters are taken out of the singer's name

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Christina Aguilera lacks the courage to sack a fellow performer with a temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping RA from AGUILERA leaves AGUILE, whose middle IL is then removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is an old word for a malarial fever with fits of shivering.

clue.text: Lines written by Queen are covered by Kiss mostly. They make hits

indicators.note: being covered by means the lines and queen sit inside the trimmed kiss
mostly means the band name loses its final letter
written by places the queen's letters after the lines

parts.note: L is a line, so LL is lines
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A song by Queen gets covered by the band Kiss, and the result is a string of chart hits.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen, Kiss and The Killers are all bands; a cover is a new version of another act's song.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit is slang for an assassination, so assassins are the ones who carry out hits.

clue.text: Fine music centre on which you put 1000…0 Maniacs

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece on another places it above, so it comes first

parts.note: 1000 is K, the kilo, followed by 0 as the letter O
OK means fine

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word music

explanation.surface: A hi-fi music centre plays a record by the band 10,000 Maniacs.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 1000…0 echoes 10,000 Maniacs, the US band; The Kooks are a British band.
explanation.definitionFit: A kook is informal US slang for an eccentric or crazy person, so kooks are madmen.

clue.text: See 20
Bands you heard featured in poster with New Order

indicators.note: featured in means the sound-alike letter appears inside the rearranged word
putting a word into a new order means rearranging its letters
heard says the word you is taken as it sounds, the letter U

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A gig poster advertises a band alongside New Order.
explanation.walkthrough: New Order is a Manchester band; here it signals the anagram of POSTER, TROPES.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of performers, so bands of players or entertainers fit.

clue.text: Union J has nothing against One Direction

indicators.note: against puts the next pieces up beside the ones before

parts.note: O is the round zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral one
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: The boy band Union J holds nothing against rivals One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Union J and One Direction were both boy bands from The X Factor.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joint or point of connection, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Front of Abbey Rd LP designed with men to have walked over

indicators.note: designed means the letters are worked into a new arrangement
front of picks the opening letter of the word Abbey

explanation.surface: The cover of the Beatles' Abbey Road album was designed around men walking across a zebra crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Abbey Road LP cover shows the Beatles crossing a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread heavily over something or someone is to walk all over it, crushing it underfoot.

clue.text: Doctor Dre's Beats losing bass, it's claimed

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
losing means a letter is dropped from the brand words

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A review says Dr Dre's Beats headphones are weak on the low end.
explanation.walkthrough: Beats is Dr Dre's headphone brand; 'Doctor' looks like his title but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to state it forcefully as true, the same as to claim it.

clue.text: Trades in Slade remixes

indicators.note: remixes says the band name's letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A record shop sells remixed tracks by the glam rock band Slade.
explanation.definitionFit: Deals are transactions or bargains, the same as trades between two parties.

clue.text: Tupac is oddly making a comeback. After vacation, RiRi's penned lines for performer

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the singer's piece is held inside
making a comeback means those picked letters are read backwards
oddly takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of those words
after vacation the inside of the name is emptied, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A rapper returns from the dead, and Rihanna, back from holiday, has written him a song.
explanation.walkthrough: RiRi is Rihanna's nickname; Tupac is the late rapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text of what an actor speaks, the words given to a player.

clue.text: How to twerk where you can't get any lower

definitions.meaning: twerking is a dance done by shaking one's backside, rocking the rear

definitions.text: where you can't get any lower
definitions.meaning: the lowest possible level, a nadir

explanation.surface: Twerking is the dance that marks the lowest point of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the lowest possible point, and read literally it means swinging one's backside.

clue.text: Turn on mike. Sound's beginning to echo and reflect

indicators.note: on places the turn piece next to the mike letter, after it

parts.note: M is mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a U-turn, so U is a turn

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word sound

parts.note: E is echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A singer switches on the microphone and starts the sound with reverb.
explanation.walkthrough: Muse is also a rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or think deeply, the same as reflecting on something.

clue.text: Number one French melody to date is not in key

parts.note: un is the French for the number one
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: The best French song so far is sung off-key.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that has not been tuned plays out of tune, off the correct pitch.

clue.text: Dave's partner's electronic track

parts.note: Chas and Dave were a London singing duo, so Dave's partner is Chas
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Chas of Chas and Dave has recorded a dance music single.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas and Dave were a Cockney rock'n'roll duo popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To track is to follow or pursue, the verb sense of going after someone.

clue.text: Indulged very large group with grandiose finale in CD

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces between the two letters of CD

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing label for very large
a set is a group

indicators.note: finale takes the closing letter of the word grandiose

explanation.surface: A big band with an over-the-top closing number indulges itself on a compact disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper someone, the same as indulging them with care and comforts.

clue.text: Finally! Music diva learns perfect pitch

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: At long last a singing diva masters perfect pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks musical, but it means throw; Cast is also a band.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a ball is to throw it, and to cast is to throw too.

clue.text: Standing during songs t.A.T.u. sang

indicators.note: during says the letters run inside those words, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: A listener stands up while the Russian duo t.A.T.u. are singing.
explanation.walkthrough: t.A.T.u. were a Russian pop duo; Status Quo are a British band.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's position or rank in society, one's social standing.

clue.text: Cocktail punch is for Coldplay

parts.note: a snowball is a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade
to punch is to hit, to fight

explanation.surface: A drinks list says the band Coldplay drink cocktail and punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Coldplay is a British band; read as cold play it is a game in the snow. Cocktail and punch both look like drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling packed snow at each other is a playful game held in freezing weather, play in the cold.

clue.text: Musical instruments of interest to Fine Young Cannibals or Doctor & the Medics?

definitions.meaning: pipe instruments played with keyboards in churches

definitions.text: of interest to Fine Young Cannibals or Doctor & the Medics?
definitions.meaning: body parts, which cannibals eat and doctors treat

explanation.surface: Bands named after cannibals and doctors care about their instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine Young Cannibals and Doctor & the Medics are 1980s bands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both keyboard pipe instruments and the heart, liver and other body parts.

clue.text: U2 guitarist got left on the shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so L comes first

parts.note: The Edge is the guitarist of the Irish band U2

explanation.surface: U2's guitarist was left on the shelf, unwanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow flat projection from a wall, essentially a shelf of rock or wood.

clue.text: Very loud arrangement of dire song about one who's looking for drugs

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap around the loud pair
an arrangement of music reworks it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A noisy cover of a terrible song is about someone after drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained police animal that sniffs out narcotics at airports is searching for illegal drugs.

clue.text: Head of Factory set up A&R meeting with Andy and Shed 7

indicators.note: with joins the name's leftover to what came before
head of picks the first letter of the label's name
in a down clue set up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: A and R, the record industry talent scouts, give the two letters

indicators.note: shed means the little word inside the name is cast off

parts.note: the word and is what the name loses

explanation.surface: Factory Records' boss arranges an A&R meeting with Andy and the band Shed Seven.
explanation.walkthrough: Factory was a Manchester record label; Shed Seven a York band. Andy shedding AND leaves Y; The Fray is a band too.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a battle or skirmish, a hostile clash where fighters engage one another.

clue.text: 1D turned to Simon Cowell initially to produce record

indicators.note: turned means the band's short name is flipped round

parts.note: 1D is short for One Direction, read as the letters I and D

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each name

explanation.surface: One Direction turned to Simon Cowell first to make a record.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Cowell launched One Direction on The X Factor.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, a flat circle of vinyl.

clue.text: Rock 'n' rollers from the 50s respect Ed Sheeran to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Old-time rockers grudgingly admit some admiration for Ed Sheeran.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth cult with Edwardian-style suits and a love of rock 'n' roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Teds is short for Teddy boys, the 1950s British youths devoted to that early music.

clue.text: After Diamonds by Rihanna ends, Kanye heartlessly makes boy duck

indicators.note: after says the rapper's letters follow the rest
by places the singer's letters beside the suit letter

parts.note: D is diamonds, the card suit

indicators.note: ends takes the outside letters of the singer's name
heartlessly removes the whole middle of the name, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: After Rihanna's song Diamonds ends, Kanye cruelly makes a boy dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds is a Rihanna song; Drake is also a rapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is the male of the duck, so the boy among ducks.

clue.text: Faint hint of narcissism displayed in Syco: training is required

indicators.note: displayed in means the hint letter is shown inside the label's name
a hint of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: PE is physical education, training

explanation.surface: Simon Cowell's label Syco shows a trace of vanity, and its artists must be coached.
explanation.walkthrough: Syco is Simon Cowell's record label. 'Faint' looks like an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Syncope is the medical term for a fainting fit, a brief loss of consciousness.
